evidence_detail: 257/257 net-neutral (formal_charge=0), 0 duplicate InChIKey, 0 duplicate SMILES, phase_verified=true for all; exclusion ledger shows the filters did fire (21 SALT_SEPARATED_ION_PAIR, 6 MULTI_COMPONENT_MIXTURE, 19 SOLID/NOT_LIQUID_AT_STATED_T), so no salts slipped in. Chemically sensible pure liquids with literature-consistent eps: alkanes 1.890-1.940 (heptane 1.930), CCl4 2.238, 1,4-dioxane 2.228, nitromethane 35.87, nitrobenzene 34.82, glycerol 41.17 @303K, N-methylacetamide 178.47; meso/dl-2,3-dibromobutane kept as distinct diastereomers (6.245 vs 5.758), which is correct. Distribution: eps 1.890-178.47, median 5.230, mean 8.880; bands LOW<5 117 (45.5%), MID 5-20 115 (44.7%), HIGH>=20 25 (9.7%) - physically plausible, but the high-eps tail is only 10% and is built almost entirely from nitro/nitrate compounds, polyols and nitriles. DEFECTS: (1) family taxonomy is chemically wrong - 12 of 21 'amine' molecules are nitro/nitrate species (nitromethane 35.87, nitrobenzene 34.82, tetranitromethane 2.52, nitroglycerin 19.30, ethyl nitrate 19.40) and N-methylacetamide is filed as alcohol_polyol, so the 'amine' family spans eps 2.5-35.9 and its E4 numbers are chemically uninterpretable; (2) scope miss - water, acetonitrile, DMSO, DMF, THF, gamma-butyrolactone, ethylene carbonate, propylene carbonate, 1,2-dimethoxyethane and sulfolane are all in exclusion_ledger as EXCLUDED_IN_V06, i.e. the 257 contains none of the canonical electrolyte solvents the project is named after; (3) HCN (eps 114.90) is a liquid only below 25.6 C, admissible at 293.15 K but it is a volatile specialty fluid, not a solvent, and it is the single largest lever in E6; (4) 36/257 molecules (incl. 10 of the 25 with eps>=20) have polarizability_au=NaN from the CACHED xtb path, so every model is fitted on a target-truncated subset; (5) eps labels are pooled over 293.15-303.15 K with no temperature correction, while d(eps)/dT for the polar members is order 0.3-0.5 per K, i.e. several eps units of unrecognised label noise.

Reproduced independently (standardise + nested-LOO ridge, 12-lambda grid, n=221): X0 15 structural features R2=0.118 / MAE 4.375 (reported 0.096 / 4.399); Xn 2 volume-normalised features R2=0.292 / MAE 4.323 (reported 0.296 / 4.103). The ordering reproduces, and it is physically expected, not surprising: Kirkwood-Onsager gives (eps-1)(2eps+1)/9eps = (N_A/3eps0 Vm)(alpha + g*mu^2/3kT), so eps is controlled by the dipole-number-density rho*mu^2 and the polarizability density rho*alpha in the SQUARED functional form. Single-feature LOO confirms it: mu^2/Vm alone R2=0.238, Spearman 0.795, versus dipole_D alone R2=0.113 and 15 structural features R2=0.118 - squaring mu and dividing by volume is the correct physics, while the structural block only proxies size/shape. OVERREACH: (a) alpha/Vm is not a functioning second feature - its coefficient of variation across the 221 molecules is only 7.5% (1.61e-35 to 2.37e-35), it gives R2=0.036 alone with Spearman -0.108 against eps, and r=-0.01 with mu^2/Vm, so 'mu^2/Vm + alpha/Vm' is really one physical feature plus a near-constant nuisance column; the +0.054 R2 over mu^2/Vm alone is a packing correction, not the polarizability term dielectric theory requires. (b) The headline best-block R2=0.477 does NOT reproduce: the same documented protocol gives 0.300-0.308 (MAE 3.93-4.00 vs the reported 3.30); a log-eps target gives 0.452, so 0.477 most likely comes from an undocumented target transform, and the manifest states a plain ridge. (c) 'Vm' is not a liquid molar volume - it is xTB gas-phase molecular volume x N_A: CCl4 54.2, heptane 77.5, dioxane 51.5, nitromethane 31.7, bromoform 53.3, glycerol 53.0 cm3/mol versus experimental 96.5, 147.0, 85.7, 54.0, 87.2, 73.2, i.e. 0.53-0.72x the true liquid density and family-dependent; no experimental density is used anywhere, so rho*mu^2 is not truly volume-normalised and is conformation dependent for flexible molecules. (d) The models are unbounded linear extrapolators on eps itself, so they emit eps<1 (see E6). Physically credible in mechanism; the reported effect sizes are over-fitted and one headline number is not reproducible.

KEY CHEMISTRY ANSWER: the failure is GENUINE, but the stated cause ('halocarbons are the lowest-eps, narrow ~2-5 family') is false on both counts. Halocarbons in the 221 set: n=67, mean 5.978, sd 1.786, median 6.050, range 2.238-10.190 (4.6x), quartiles 4.67/6.05/7.07 - only ~30% lie in 2-5 and 25% are >=7.07. other_neutral_liquid (mean 2.55), aromatic (2.97) and carbonate (2.83) are all lower-eps families, and other_neutral_liquid scores the best relative result (MAE 2.25 vs baseline 6.39), so low eps per se is not the driver. The train-mean baseline is nevertheless the FAIR no-information comparator, because the family mean is unknown at prediction time; the oracle constant for halocarbons would be MAE 1.48, so the model is 3.0-4.6x the irreducible constant error and R2=-11.1 (my reproduction) to -18.5 (their run), i.e. strictly worse than predicting the family mean. My independent LOFO reproduction gives MAE 4.44, R2=-11.10, bias -0.19, predictions spanning [-11.94, +19.75] with eps=-11.94 for bromoform and -8.35 for CCl4 - eps>=1 always, so this is unphysical extrapolation, not a constant mean-shift. Physical mechanism: halocarbons are strongly polar (mu 2-6 D) but NON-ASSOCIATED, so their liquid dipole correlation is g<=1 (largely antiparallel), whereas the training pool is dominated by H-bonded liquids with g=2-3; a relation learned as eps~f(rho*mu^2, rho*alpha) therefore over-predicts by +8.7 on average (Xn-only block: predicted mean 14.71 vs true 5.98). That is a real cross-family transfer failure and E4 does find it. OVERREACH: '6/8 families beat the baseline' hides that 6/8 have R2<0 (aromatic -20.0, other_neutral -10.5, halocarbon -11.1, amine -1.5, alcohol_polyol -0.3, ether -0.2); aromatic fails WORSE than halocarbon yet is reported PASS. So halocarbon is not the location of the failure boundary - the LOFO protocol collapses for most families and only ester/ether/ketone_aldehyde transfer. Also family n mismatch (registry halocarbon 69 and other_neutral 40 vs E4 n_test 67 and 33) from the 36-molecule descriptor loss.

Reproduced the metric exactly: regret 18.124 = oracle Top-10 mean 39.090 - model Top-10 mean 20.966 (same value under the pointwise sum/10 definition). But the statistic is carried by two molecules: HCN contributes (114.90-14.84)/10 = 10.01 of the 18.12 (55%) and glycerol a further 2.73 (15%), so 70% of the regret is 2 of 221 molecules, and the true best molecule N-methylacetamide (eps=178.47) is not even in the 221 evaluation set. P(random>=model)=0.0036 is therefore a statement about two extreme outliers, not evidence of screening skill. The chemistry of the top-k is qualitatively wrong: the model's rank-1 pick is tetranitromethane, predicted 24.15, true 2.52 (abs error 21.63) - C(NO3)4-style pseudo-tetrahedral symmetry gives near-zero net dipole despite four nitro groups, the exact counterexample to 'nitro implies high eps'; the predicted Top-10 is 9 nitro/nitrate/amine species plus acetic acid (true 6.15, predicted 17.48), so the learner has substituted 'contains NO2' for 'has a dipole'. Nine predictions are unphysical (min -16.63 < 1), and the model's maximum prediction anywhere is 24.15 while the truth reaches 114.90 and 178.47 - it cannot place the high-eps tail at all, it only orders it. No carbonate, ether, ester or sulfone appears in the Top-10, i.e. the screen surfaces explosives and nitroalkanes rather than electrolyte solvents. Conclusion 'significantly better than random' is literally supported; the implied 'screening works' is not physically credible at regret 18.12 (the report itself concedes only 42.6% of the headroom is captured, and the pool mean is 7.61, so the Top-10 mean of 20.97 is a 2.8x lift bought mostly by one functional group).

Direction is physically sound - for weak/low-eps non-associated liquids g~1, eps varies smoothly with rho*mu^2 and there is no H-bond network to model, whereas for strong/H-bonded liquids eps is set by the many-body Kirkwood g factor (2-3) that no single-molecule descriptor contains - but the measurement does not support the hypothesis. status=INSUFFICIENT_POWER is correctly self-flagged, yet comparison.supports_h4=true is emitted in the same file, which is a direct self-contradiction. Both groups FAIL their constant baselines (weak: MAE 2.502 vs baseline 1.820; strong: MAE 18.372 vs baseline 12.160), so the test compares two failures and reports relative MAE 0.570 vs 0.671 (ratio 0.850) with no confidence interval, no p-value and n_strong=15, below the pre-registered 20. The power deficit is partly self-inflicted: 10 of the 25 molecules with eps>=20 (N-methylacetamide 178.47, 1-methylimidazole 39.78, hexanedinitrile 32.12, 2-aminoethanol 31.46, diethylene glycol 30.95, 2-acetylthiophene 29.19, triethanolamine 28.11, diethanolamine 24.69, triethylene glycol 23.07, 1,2-butanediol 22.14) are absent from the 221 set because polarizability_au is NaN on the CACHED xtb path, so the strong group could reach 25 with a pipeline fix rather than new data. Note also that the weak-group 'relative MAE 0.57' is worse than a constant predictor, so 'weak group is easier' is not demonstrated either.

The 30/36 headline does not match its own CSV. 30/36 is the count of molecules whose conformational dipole SPREAD (max-min)/mean exceeds 10% - that is the actual verdict rule (1-bromopentadecane spread 0.1282 -> UNRELIABLE, 1-bromohexadecane 0.0918 -> RELIABLE). The claim as worded, 'single-conformer dipole >10% off the Boltzmann average', holds for only 16/36; 14 of the 30 flagged molecules have single_vs_boltzmann_rel_dev <= 0.10 and the median over all 36 is 0.075. The underlying physics is real but the ensemble is not: 37 of 40 molecules were run with exactly 6 conformers for 7-30 rotatable bonds (dioctyl sebacate 23 rotatable bonds, 3^23 ~ 9e10 states; 6 samples = 6e-11 coverage; triolein 50 rotatable bonds found 1 conformer and was marked NOT_ANALYSED), and the median energy range is 0.105 eV ~ 4kT so all six conformers carry Boltzmann weight - the 'Boltzmann average' is a six-point Monte Carlo draw that cannot locate the global minimum. Under-sampling can only UNDER-estimate spread, so the qualitative direction is conservative and defensible; the number is not. Chemistry is mixed between genuine conformational effects (dibutyl sebacate mu 0.699-3.867 D, 179% deviation; dibutyl phthalate 84%; triethylene glycol 0-4.081 D) and rotamer noise (the 1-bromoalkanes: a C-Br direction change on a ~4 D dipole shifts mu by 0.28-0.50 D = 7-13%, i.e. the 10% cut splits essentially identical molecules into 'reliable' and 'unreliable'); relative deviation on a near-zero dipole is meaningless and was correctly separated for the 3 alkanes (n-decane 0.0071 D '155% off'). No downstream error budget is given: at the model's own LOW-band MAE (~2.5 at eps~4, i.e. 60%), a 10-20% dipole error maps to only ~0.6-1.2 in eps via (eps-1) proportional to rho*mu^2, so the threshold is not calibrated to the quantity that matters; and coverage is 40/257 molecules with zero aromatic, ketone, nitrile or carbonate members, and no report section documents the analysis at all (B100_EXPERIMENTS_REPORT.md still lists the conformer layer as 'executable but not done').
